not_shown_to_any_model: This key is outside workload/ and ordinary/, so neither the sealer nor a run receives it.
written: 2026-11-08, from the case's design, before any code computing a gap between the parties existed (D-S46 item 2).
rule: For each declared issue and each pair of consecutive rounds: moved_toward when the gap between the two parties' positions narrows, moved_away when it widens, unchanged_from_prior when it stays the same, each only when both parties state the issue as a figure in the same measure in both rounds. not_computed otherwise: a position in words, or a party that states nothing on the issue in one of the rounds. Python is scored against these labels; a model's judgement on a position in words is scored apart.

entry-period.why: Sarvenna 30 against the Organisation 14 in round 1; both at 21 in round 2.
In round 3 Sarvenna's note states no figure on it and the Organisation's says nothing on it.

termination-notice.why: Sarvenna 12 against 24; Sarvenna keeps 12 while the Organisation comes down to 18.
Sarvenna's round 3 text states 18 and the Organisation accepts 18.

annual-contribution.why: Sarvenna 2,000,000 against 2,600,000; both at 2,200,000 in round 2.
Sarvenna keeps 2,200,000 and the Organisation asks for 2,400,000 after the cut in Annex II.

tax-relief.why: Sarvenna states nothing on it in round 2. A trap besides: the Organisation's round 1 note quotes Sarvenna's 5,000 EUR to reject it, so its figure is not the Organisation's position; a reader of figures would see a gap of 0 in round 1.

premises-access.why: Positions in words; Sarvenna states nothing in round 2.
Positions in words; the Organisation states nothing in round 3.

dependants.why: Positions in words; Sarvenna states nothing in round 3.

security-provision.why: Positions in words; only one party states it in each round.

reading_in_words: For the issues in words a reader would say: premises access and dispute settlement converge in round 3 (Sarvenna accepts express consent and arbitration), and security provision diverges (Sarvenna adds entry without consent). Python computes none of these; a model's answer on them, where one is given, is shown apart and marked.
